title: Extend bounded normalization through telescope cones
statement: Let $f:Z\to Y$ be a proper morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], with module-sheaf derived categories in a common universe [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $F=L f^*$ be the recorded derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback], supplied with a strong monoidal structure for the recorded derived tensors [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], and suppose termwise tensor pullback $H=f^*$ is additive [def-pc-module-pullback]. Write $q_Y$ for the homotopy quotient, $Q_Y,Q_Z$ for localization, $L=Q_YF$, and $G=H^hQ_Z$. Write $c_X(K):\mathcal O_X[1]\otimes K\cong K[1]$ for the canonical first-variable Koszul comparison followed by the translated left unitor [def-sc-scheme-canonical-shift-unit-iso], and $\delta_F$ for the supplied inverse tensorator. For an isomorphism $e:F(\mathcal O_Y[1])\cong\mathcal O_Z[1]$ put $b_e(K)=F(c_Y(K)^{-1});\delta_F(\mathcal O_Y[1],K);(e\otimes\mathrm{id});c_Z(F(K))$. Fix $e$ as above and isomorphisms $\beta_X:L(X)\cong G(X)$ for every $X$ in $B_Y$ [def-sc-bounded-flat-shift-representative]. Assume $L(s);\beta_{X'}=\beta_X;G(s)$ for every homotopy map between objects in $B_Y$, and assume $\beta_{X[1]};\mathrm{commShift}_G(X)=F(\mathrm{commShift}_{Q_Y}(X));b_e(Q_YX);\beta_X[1]$ whenever $X=q_Y(P)$ with $P$ bounded above and termwise flat. Then there exist isomorphisms $\alpha_X:L(X)\cong G(X)$ for every flat telescope shift representative $X$ [def-sc-flat-telescope-stage-map], natural for stage-induced maps: $L(s);\alpha_{X'}=\alpha_X;G(s)$. For every literal flat telescope $P$, $X=q_Y(P)$ satisfies $\alpha_{X[1]};\mathrm{commShift}_G(X)=F(\mathrm{commShift}_{Q_Y}(X));b_e(Q_YX);\alpha_X[1]$. The input $e$ is retained; no new translated-unit comparison is chosen and no naturality outside the model class is asserted.

proof.text: Construct the stage-natural normalized forward morphisms a, with agreement with beta on bounded telescope representatives.

Agreement with the supplied bounded isomorphisms proves IsIso on bounded representatives. Common-refinement cancellation extends stage naturality to all homotopy maps between the representatives, supplying the naturality hypothesis of telescope invertibility propagation. Package each component with asIso; the required stage naturality and shift equations are definitionally the original forward-map equations.
